остановиться.gloss: to stop, to come to a halt

meanings.en: to stop, to come to a halt
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stop, to come to a halt', paired with 'останавливаться'.

examples.text: Он только начал бояться, а ты остановился!
examples.trans: He just started getting scared, and you stopped!
Has the bleeding stopped yet?

examples.text: Ваня, ты что? Он только начал бояться, а ты остановился!
examples.trans: Vanya, what is wrong with you? He just started getting scared, and you stopped!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'chaos, mess' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We stopped in a rundown little village.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый хаус.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new chaos.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'small village, hamlet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We stopped in a rundown little village.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая деревушка.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new small village.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want, feel like', paired with 'захотеться'.

examples.text: Самсоновы, ну вы очнитесь! Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: Samsonovs, come to your senses! I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: Я понимаю, вам очень хочется квартиру.
examples.trans: I understand you really want the flat.

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?
I met him by chance.

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Извините, а вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Hello! Excuse me, are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.trans: Where will I find movers?
I found the phone.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'jar, can, tin' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The supplier will bring the jar in an hour.
Hide the jar under the table!

examples.text: Шеф ничего не узнает, прячь банку!
examples.trans: Chef will not find out anything, hide the jar!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'tuna' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И тут я случайно нашел банку тунца.
examples.trans: And then by chance I found a can of tuna.
A little bit of tuna.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('village, country, rustic').

examples.trans: So I decided to make a rustic village salad.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень деревенский день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very village day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алат'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salad' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a salad.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.

examples.text: Гость пришёл специально ради этого салата.
examples.trans: The guest came especially for this salad.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: I'm not taking the knife.
Chef, I didn't take it.
We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fox' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We take a lettuce leaf.
Guys, I forgot to update the eighty-six list.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Don't talk so rudely.
That's rude.

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to tear, rush ahead'.

examples.trans: We tear it roughly just like this.
You simply cannot take your eyes off them.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.
There, look.
You'll see!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does this mean?
So you're not coming.
Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, after that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Затем мы подпишем все официальные документы.
examples.trans: Then we will sign all official documents.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to add, supplement'.

examples.text: Я добавляю свежую зелень и соус.
examples.trans: I add fresh greens and sauce.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.
Add the dye slowly and carefully.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'пелиный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('quail (eggs)').

examples.trans: Next we add some quail eggs.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень перепелиный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very quail day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'egg' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'множко'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Wait a little.
I need to work a little.

examples.text: Мне нужно немножко поработать с бывшим мэром.
examples.trans: I need to do a little work on the former mayor.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'olive' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A few olives.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая оливка.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new olive.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'potato, potatoes' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: How could we do without potatoes.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый картофель.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new potato.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'перчить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pepper, season with pepper'.

examples.trans: We pepper the whole thing.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет поперчить без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to pepper without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Take care, I love you.
Take care, I love you!

мешать.gloss: to be in the way, to disturb

meanings.en: to be in the way, to disturb
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be in the way, to disturb', paired with 'помешать'.

examples.trans: The radiators are in the way.
Don't bother me!

examples.text: Филиппыч, миксер проехать не может. Радиаторы мешают.
examples.trans: Filippych, the mixer truck can't get through. The radiators are in the way.
